title: For a smooth equidimensional scheme over a field the bivariant Chow ring is Chow homology and composition becomes intersection
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a field k and a smooth scheme X over k equidimensional of dimension d, the lemma asserts that c -> c cap [X]_d is an isomorphism A^p(X) -> CH_{d-p}(X) and that under it composition of bivariant classes becomes the intersection product (statement lines 14402-14412). The proof writes the map as a composition of two isomorphisms A^p(X) -> A^{p-d}(X -> Spec(k)) -> CH_{d-p}(X), the first being c -> c o g^* from Proposition labelled proposition-compute-bivariant and the second c -> c cap [Spec(k)] from Lemma labelled lemma-chow-cohomology-towards-point (proof lines 14414-14422). It then reads the inverses off the proofs of those two results: the inverse of the second sends alpha to the class c_alpha acting by beta -> alpha x beta in CH_*(X x_k Y), and the inverse of the first sends c_alpha to the class acting by beta -> Delta^!(alpha x beta) = alpha . beta, which identifies composition with the intersection product (proof lines 14424-14434). Chasing the two explicit inverses to see that composition corresponds to the diagonal product is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
